evidence.claim: Dink! Pickleball Round Robins sells Premium Annual for $24.99 and Premium Permanent access for $39.99 as in-app purchases, with 17 ratings averaging 4.6.
Pickleheads charges players $19.99 a year or $2.99 a month for Plus, which unlocks unlimited round robins, tournaments, leagues and ladders for organisers.
Pickleheads pricing page caps free and Plus accounts at 2 round robins a month, sells extra round robins at $5 each, and charges organisers $14.99 a month for Pro with 10 a month.
DinkDrop Pickleball Round Robin on the US App Store sells Pickleball Pro in-app purchases at $2.99, $19.99 and $44.99, rated 4.5 from 11 ratings.
SFIA reports 24.3 million Americans aged 6 and older played pickleball in 2025, up from 4.2 million in 2020.
The Pickleheads round robin tool page shows a 4.9 app rating from 9.2k reviews and a facility with nearly 500 players using it, so organisers actively use round robin software.

title: Rally Rounds
oneLiner: Pickleball round robin schedules and live scores for club organisers, no app install
customer: Volunteer pickleball and padel session organisers
revenueModel: Free for small sessions, paid organiser pass
nextAction: Business case by research, then sizing, then CEO go or no-go. Against: Reclub is free with live scores, Pickleheads gives 2 free round robins a month and has 9.2k reviews; the paid gap is narrow (no install, no account, cheaper than $5 per extra event).

lead.trait: Lets the numbers decide what to cut.

evidenceAgainst.claim: Reclub describes itself as a free-to-use app with round robin generation, live scoring and live standings for up to 8 courts and 24 players.
Pickleball Scheduler on the US App Store is free with no listed in-app purchases (3.7 from 3 ratings).
Pickleheads gives every free account 2 round robins a month, so casual organisers already have a free option from a dominant brand.
